Used for for the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer in patients who have previously received chemotherapy, anti-EGFR or anti-VEGF therapy. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor and a hepatotoxic agent. It is a member of phenylureas, a pyridinecarboxamide, an aromatic ether, a member of monochlorobenzenes, a member of (trifluoromethyl)benzenes and a member of monofluorobenzenes.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:68647"}], "BRD-K56195681": [{"source_id": "pubchem:11552706:description:1", "text": "Losmapimod is a secondary carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 6-[5-(cyclopropylcarbamoyl)-3-fluoro-2-methylphenyl]pyridine-3-carboxylic acid with the amino group of neopentylamine. It is a potent p38alpha/beta mitogen activated protein kinase inhibitor which was previously in clinical trials for the treatment of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy trial now discontinued due to not achieving its primary endpoint. It has a role as a nootropic agent, an anti-inflammatory agent, a cardioprotective agent and an EC 2.7.11.24 (mitogen-activated protein kinase) inhibitor. It is a secondary carboxamide, a member of benzamides, a pyridinecarboxamide, a member of toluenes, a phenylpyridine, a member of cyclopropanes and a member of monofluorobenzenes.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:131167"}], "BRD-K70301465": [{"source_id": "pubchem:24821094:description:1", "text": "Ibrutinib is a member of the class of acrylamides that is (3R)-3-[4-amino-3-(4-phenoxyphenyl)pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidin-1-yl]piperidine in which the piperidine nitrogen is replaced by an acryloyl group. A selective and covalent inhibitor of the enzyme Bruton's tyrosine kinase, it is used for treatment of B-cell malignancies. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and an EC 2.7.10.2 (non-specific protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor. It is a tertiary carboxamide, a member of acrylamides, an aromatic amine, an aromatic ether, a pyrazolopyrimidine and a N-acylpiperidine.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:76612"}]}, "task": "Revise donor support. donors.reason: Indolecarboxamide with EZH2-inhibitor-like scaffold; closest structural analog to GSK126 among retrieved donors.
Thienopyrimidine N-arylpiperazine; high anchor similarity but no epigenetic mechanism described.
Tyrosine kinase inhibitor; high anchor similarity but no direct histone-methylation mechanism.
p38 MAPK inhibitor; moderate anchor similarity, plausible indirect chromatin effects.
BTK inhibitor; moderate anchor similarity, no epigenetic mechanism described.

revised_hypotheses: GSK126 EZH2 inhibition should reduce H3K27me3 and related H3K27me2/me3 marks while increasing lower methylation states such as H3K27me0K36me3.
CPI-169 analog BRD-A48881734 is the most mechanistically plausible donor for transferring an EZH2-inhibition histone signature.
Non-epigenetic donors with high anchor similarity may transfer shared downstream chromatin effects but lack direct H3K27me3 evidence.
The fixed decoder selects MCF7/BI10041 sign -1, so donor support should be judged by reproducible H3K27me2K36me2 decrease.
unresolved: No measured donor histone response values are supplied, so reproducible >0.5 log2 perturbation versus vehicle cannot be confirmed.
Pharmacology descriptions do not establish context-specific histone responses in A375 or the decoder target line.
Whether non-epigenetic donors share a transferable chromatin signature remains untested.
